implementation_notes: Scala has no try-with-resources syntax, so the stdlib provides scala.util.Using (since 2.13): Using.apply(resource)(f) opens the resource, runs the function and releases in reverse creation order, wrapping the whole thing in Try and merging exceptions by severity - a close failure becomes a suppressed exception on the body failure rather than replacing it. Using.Manager manages several resources with implicit registration (resources acquired during construction are released even if construction fails midway - the documented pattern is a case class that registers itself), and Using.resource throws instead of returning Try when the caller does not want the wrapper. Ownership and idempotence of the underlying close() stay the resource's responsibility: a Scala owner implements AutoCloseable and cascades to owned fields.
pitfalls: Using wraps the result in Try, which clashes with callers expecting the raw exception or a different effect type - use Using.resource or unwrap explicitly.
Resources are released only after they have been registered; relying on plain construction inside Using.Manager without use(...) leaves the resource unmanaged.
The block's value is what Using returns, so a block with side effects and a Unit result silently changes the API shape (Try[Unit]).
